sentence boundary '. ' for literal/name pairing

column1: operator memory (opt-in SYMBOLS_TASK_OPS_MEMORY): skip an operator that rolled back on the same workspace+task hash; order by remembered net success
OpenCode child-session shape: tools declared, none named task or todowrite
file-writing tool names: edit, write, patch, multiedit, apply_patch
OpenCode parent side: delegate only when the request names 2+ files present in the workspace listing; one task per file, prompts name only their own file
per-part request text: other parts' file names removed with a joining "and"/"y"/comma
agent choice: memory net score first, ties by whole-word overlap of the agent description with "execute multiple units of work in parallel"
clean rebuild of a child's part: exit 0 and no "warning:"/"error:" in the compiler output
task output shapes of OpenCode 1.18: <task id state> with <task_result>/<task_error>, or "task_id:" line with <task_result>
subagent memory (opt-in SYMBOLS_SUBAGENT_MEMORY): verified +1, failed -1 per agent and file extension; net <= -2 for a part's best agent = do it directly
missing ';' repair: gcc "expected ';' before" / "expected ',' or ';' before" at a line start appends ';' to the previous non-empty line
include from gcc note: "note: include '<h>'" adds #include <h> after the last #include
build/check output fails on "error:", "warning:", AddressSanitizer or "Assertion"; warnings-only is not a pass

explicit @agent: a user message carrying OpenCode 1.18 "call the task tool with subagent: <name>" with <name> in the task tool agent list delegates even one named workspace file to that agent (overrides agent choice and memory; needs 1+ named listed file)

doc_sync term shapes: flag "-x"/"--name", call "name(...)", identifier with "_" or a digit for the stale term A (B: any identifier of 3+ chars, not a C keyword); doc files = .md/.txt/.rst/README*, code = .c/.h

doc_sync: exactly one task term in docs and absent from every C source, exactly one same-shape task term present in a C source; replace in doc files only; verify A gone from docs and B present; named sources need not be touched
remove_dead_function cue: the sentence naming the function contains remove/delete/drop/eliminate and no "must not"/"do not"/"don't"

remove_dead_function: exactly one named function defined once in C sources and otherwise only in file-scope prototype lines; remove definition (line start to matching brace) and prototypes; verify name gone, build ok, stdout unchanged

unmatched_brace: build fails and exactly one "}" in the C sources closes nothing (depth outside comments/strings/chars would go below 0, no unclosed "{"); remove it (its line when alone); verify build goes failing -> ok
change cue: unquoted text after "change to"/"change it to" (first letter any case) up to the sentence end is treated as a quoted fragment for stated_fragment

author_test: exactly one named .c file that does not exist, exactly one task function declared in a workspace header, expected = first integer after the call in its sentence; a written call with literal-only arguments wins; else arguments from the prototype (int-like -> 1, char pointer -> "abc", other types abstain); verify: test builds with the no-main sources and exits 0; runs first in the operator order

declare_implicit system header: when no workspace file declares or defines the implicitly used function, insert the header named by gcc's note "include '<X>' or provide a declaration of 'name'"; verify fewer implicit uses and build ok
rename grounding: a plain task word (>= 3 chars, not a C keyword or main) counts as a code name when the workspace defines it as a file-level function

relop_search: program builds and exits non-zero (not timeout); swaps only on lines holding a task anchor (code-shaped or workspace-defined identifier the workspace uses) or inside the body of a function whose head holds one, no anchor = abstain; try single swaps among < <= > >= in non-test C sources (not preprocessor/comment lines), tiers 1 boundary, 2 direction, 3 rest; first tier with exactly one swap that exits 0 wins, two = abstain; max 64 builds; equality never swapped
named files: a file name right after '<' (<hdr.h>) is a system header, not a workspace file the edit must leave existing
induction trace features (phase 1, SYMBOLS_TRACE only): compile/run result before any edit plus the first gcc -Wall diagnostic line with quoted names masked to X and digit runs to N; no task wording

mutation corpus primitives (phase 2, training only): relop < <= > >= swap, binary + <-> -, && <-> ||, integer literal +1/-1, outside preprocessor lines/comments/strings; max 12 mutants per source; caught = build fails or exit != 0
mutation corpus --anchor: task text names the enclosing function of the mutated line (nearest column-0 definition head above it), never the primitive or line

stated-example oracle (phase 3a): task text calls written as f(ints) == N or f(...) expect N, f defined in the workspace; harness links workspace sources with -Dmain=symbols_ws_main; relop_search accepts a swap only if own main exits 0 (when present) and every example holds

primitive search (phase 3b): after relational tiers 1-3, tier 4 decimal literal +1/-1, tier 5 binary +<->- (previous token a name, number or closing bracket), tier 6 &&<->||; same anchors/oracle/64 builds; lines inside main are never edited when the own exit code is the oracle

definition-question drift guard: for "que es X?"/"what is X?" a quoted corpus sentence must contain X, or define its dictionary translation / marked substitute (X is|are|was|means|es|son|significa); else quote the corpus sentence defining the translation, marked [tr]; else abstain
sanitizer-aware timing: in __SANITIZE_ADDRESS__ builds throughput thresholds print [SKIP] with the measured value; functional checks still count; TPS asserts rate > 0
